title: litho-rollout-tempo-and-annotated-release-brief
content:
Summary:
This doc is a compact two-week tempo for the Litho service rollout (canary -> regional -> global) plus an annotated draft of the release notes. It's intentionally lightweight for the ops crew: clear daily beats, precise telemetry gates, and a short rollback decision ladder. Use this as the single source for launch-day shifts and the first 72 hours of stabilization.

TL;DR goals:
- Launch Litho v2.1 behind feature gate F-LITHO-21 with staged traffic ramp (0.5% -> 10% -> 50% -> 100%).
- Maintain 95th percentile latency <= 160ms for critical /generate routes.
- Error budget burn <= 5% during the 48h observation window.
- No customer-facing regression in embeddings or chat-quality top-3 prompts (tracked by eval harness).

Success metrics and signal owners:
- Latency (p95 /generate): target <= 160ms. Owner: Ethan Park (observability).
- Error rate (5xx + model-timeout): max 0.5% at 10% traffic; owner: SRE on-call.
- Cost delta anomaly (tokens / minute): owner: FinOps (Roxanne Li) - notify if +15% vs projected.
- Quality regressions (eval-suite): owner: Applied ML (Samir) - auto-alert on >1.5% drop on benchmark prompts.

Preflight quick-run checklist (48–24 hours):
- [ ] Canary image built and verified: litho:v2.1. Sha: (from GH-PR 452 CI).
- [ ] Model variant matrix mapped and pinned for fallback (quantized fallback available).
- [ ] Smoke harness: local smoke-run passes (10 sample flows) — owner: release engineer.
- [ ] Traffic steering policies preloaded in routing service; dry-run verified.
- [ ] KMS rotation window clear; secrets env validated in staging.
- [ ] Observability: dashboards created + template alert rules staged, alert paging tested.
- [ ] Postmortem playbook stub attached to incident channel (#launch-litho).

Two-week rollout calendar (condensed):
Week 0 (preflight) - Mon/Tue:
- Mon: Final build verification; integration smoke; toggle off auto-scalers to test baseline capacity; dry-run in staging.
- Tue: Canary deployment to us-west-2 (single AZ) at 09:00 PT; initial canary traffic 0.5% 10:00–13:00 (monitor p95/err).

Week 1 (staged regional ramp) - Wed/Fri:
- Wed: If canary signals OK, ramp to 2% at 09:00 PT; keep flat 2% for 4 hours. P95 check and ops signoff at +4h.
- Thu: Hold day / buffer for rollbacks or fixes.
- Fri: Regional ramp to 10% at 09:00 PT across us-west/us-east with careful routing policy; 2-hour soak, then decision.

Weekend (safety window):
- Sat: No scheduled ramps. Watch window 12:00–18:00 PT; light monitoring crew.
- Sun: Optional sprint to address hotfixes; no traffic increases unless explicitly approved by release lead.

Week 2 (global roll) - Mon/Tue:
- Mon: If regional stable, ramp to 50% across regions at 08:00 PT with progressive rollout to additional clusters over 3 hours.
- Tue: Final sweep to 100% at 10:00 PT if all gates green; start 72h heightened observation window.

Operator cues and checklist for each ramp step:
- Pre-ramp (30m): ensure on-call roster present; confirm alerting silence for unrelated services; snapshot of dashboards saved.
- T+10m: quick sanity check: p95, error rate, CPU of inference nodes.
- T+60m: run a sampled prompt-correctness job vs control dataset; expect similarity score >= 0.98.
- If anomaly: immediate throttle to previous steady traffic percentage and escalate to release lead.

Telemetry gates (gating thresholds that trigger hold/rollback):
- Gate 1 (p95 latency): if p95 > 220ms for 3 consecutive 5m windows -> hold and revert to prior traffic level.
- Gate 2 (Error spike): if 5xx rate > 1.0% sustained for 10m -> rollback to previous stage and wake SRE.
- Gate 3 (Quality): if eval-suite shows >2.0% regression on top-3 prompts -> stop ramp, route traffic to fallback model, notify Applied ML.
- Gate 4 (Cost): sudden >25% token cost anomaly in 30m -> pause ramp, open FinOps channel.

Rollback decision ladder (fast path):
- Level 0 (auto-throttle): routing layer reduces new-canary allocation by 80% (automatic).
- Level 1 (manual fast rollback): release engineer triggers immediate global route revert to stable image. Time-to-complete target: < 6 minutes.
- Level 2 (full rollback): if rollback fails or the root cause is infra-level (e.g., kernel panic) then initiate isolation playbook and engage infra team.

Backout & remediation steps (short):
1) Freeze all traffic changes and create incident log entry.
2) Revert routing to stable tag (stable: litho:v2.0).
3) Scale up stable instances if needed.
4) Collect debugging artifacts: heap profiles, kernel logs, model-serving traces, request dump for 10 minutes prior to anomaly.
5) Run targeted tests in a canary sandbox replicating failure window.
6) Postmortem: to be drafted within 72 hours by the incident commander.

Release notes (annotated draft for external/internal channels):
Title: Litho v2.1 — Cost and latency optimizations with stronger fallback paths\nShort blurb: This release introduces a reworked batching scheduler, improved KV-cache locality for long context sessions, and explicit fallbacks for quantized variants to reduce customer-visible timeouts during peak usage.
Notable changes:
- New: adaptive small-batch scheduler that reduces per-token latency for short prompts.
- Improved: KV cache eviction heuristics to reduce context-window misses on long chat sessions.
- Fixed: a routing race that could cause increased model flip latency under heavy concurrent requests.
- NOTE: A/B customers using dedicated routing policies may see temporary increases in cost during initial ramp (projected +8% on token spend) as caches warm. FinOps has estimated the steady-state delta to be <2%.
Known issues:
- Rare index OOB on very long (>32k tokens) requests — handled by automatic chunking, but may increase response time.
- Edge case: embeddings for small inputs may change by <0.5% similarity vs v2.0; we have verification harness in place.
Operational notes for customers (internal copy):
- Default behavior: service will attempt quantized fallback on model-timeout and serve a fast degraded result.
- For Dedicated customers: contact Solutions Eng to pin model variants or request cache warmup slots.

Post-release watchlist (first 72h):
- Every 2h: telemetry digest (p95, error rate, cost) emailed to release channel. Owner: release lead.
- Hourly: eval-suite snapshot against top-20 prompts. Owner: Applied ML.
- Shift handoff doc updated at each 8h rotation with current bookmarks and anomalies.

Open action items (owner / due):
- Samir: finalize eval-suite prompts list (due 2027-05-12).
- Ethan: create a lightweight latency dashboard with comparison to v2.0 (due 2027-05-11).
- Roxanne: approve projected cost ceiling and configure FinOps alert (due 2027-05-13).
- Priya (release lead): confirm on-call roster and update incident channel links (done 2027-05-10).

Notes to reviewers (brief):
- This doc is intentionally normative: follow the tempo, sign off each ramp step in the release channel before proceeding. If any gate trips, prefer conservative rollback.
- We'll convert the final release notes to the external template after the 72h watch completes.

Appendix (quick links):
- Smoke logs: GH-PR-452/ci/smoke 
- Canary deployment manifest: CONFLUENCE-1234/pages/litho-canary-manifest
- Incident channel: #launch-litho (alerts -> paging group Litho-OPS)

End of brief.

(Handwritten notes / scratch):
- keep weekend quiet window conservative; prefer Monday global when SRE staffing is full.
- fast rollback target must be exercised in a dry run preflight (test time-to-revert).
- consider adding a transient cache pre-warm job 30m before regional ramps.
